key_insight: The paper gives an explicit test for whether sampled data lie near a real algebraic complete intersection of fixed dimension, degree, and condition number, effectively turning a manifold-hypothesis check into a computable geometric decision problem.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for high-dimensional data analysis because it provides a principled way to detect and fit structured low-dimensional geometry when the data are assumed to live near an algebraic manifold.
method: Derive quantitative geometric bounds for regular polynomial systems.
Reduce manifold testing to an auxiliary optimization problem with controlled complexity.
Design a data-driven algorithm with explicit sample and arithmetic complexity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit bounds on sample complexity and arithmetic complexity, showing the method is analyzed algorithmically rather than only theoretically.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on strong modeling assumptions: the target set must be a real algebraic complete intersection with prescribed dimension, bounded degree, and bounded condition number.
